blocks.heading: Changing priorities
blocks.text: Business priorities can change with survival pressures, resources, demand and stakeholder concerns. A new enterprise may emphasise establishing customers; a business facing a cash shortage may prioritise paying immediate bills. Once stable, it may give more attention to expansion, product improvement or staff development. Changing priorities does not necessarily mean abandoning the longer-term objective: it may change the sequence in which objectives are pursued.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: Omuti Foods planned a larger shop, but a delivery vehicle now needs urgent repair. Reliable deliveries may become the immediate priority because existing sales depend on them. Delaying expansion can preserve cash for repairs and protect current customers. If the vehicle is repaired and cash improves, expansion can be reconsidered. A stronger explanation identifies the changed circumstance and why it alters the relative urgency of the objectives.
